idiom_name: plain { headers, body } object; Node http.IncomingMessage; broker content Buffer + options.headers
implementation_notes: No Message class is needed: a plain object literal with a headers property and a body property already is the package, and JSON serialization plus structural typing keep it transport-independent. The real message objects appear at the edges - Node's http.IncomingMessage exposes a lower-cased headers object (plus rawHeaders for the original spelling) and a Readable body stream, and broker clients package the same split, e.g. amqplib sendToQueue(content, options) takes a Buffer body plus an options object whose headers field becomes the AMQP header section and whose contentType/correlationId/messageId map to AMQP properties. A class wrapper is justified only when the project needs invariant enforcement (validated header names, binary body handling) that a plain object cannot express.
pitfalls: Never put the payload in headers: header values must be strings (or JSON-serializable) and brokers bound their size, so a Buffer in headers is silently coerced or rejected.
Node request/response bodies are single-read streams; forgetting to consume or destroy IncomingMessage keeps the socket and its memory alive, and a second 'data' listener gets nothing.
JSON round-tripping loses types: a Buffer body comes back as {type:'Buffer',data:[...]} and a Date becomes a string, so the wire encoding of the body must be agreed explicitly.
